answer: Velvet Clock Admission. Each new agent identity must submit its first N actions through a randomized admission window drawn from a shared velvet schedule; the server checks inter-arrival variance against an ivory baseline. Sybils that batch-create identities produce suspiciously uniform timing and get throttled. An attacker must pay to spread registrations across a mesa of slow, jittered windows, raising the wall-clock cost per identity by roughly an order of magnitude.
